Counsel for Applicant :- Vikas Sharma,Ambica Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anoop Chandra,Mansi Gupta,Vimal Kishor Singh Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Ambica Tripathi, learned counsel for the accused-applicant, Ms. Mansi Gupta, learned counsel appearing for the complainant/informant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Anil Kumar for grant of bail, in Complaint Case No. 1789 of 2018, under Section 363 and 376 I.P.C., Police Station Bilgram, District Hardoi, during trial.
3. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.

Initially on the application moved by the complainant under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C., under the orders of the Magistrate, first information report was lodged and after thorough investigation a 'closure report/final report' was submitted by the investigating officer.
However, on a protest petition filed by the complainant/informant, the same was treated as complaint and on the Anil Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 basis of the statement of the complainant recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and of her witnesses recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C., the applicant has been summoned along with other two accused persons to face trial under Section 363 and 376 I.P.C.
4.

It is vehemently submitted that the trial Court in a mechanical way has summoned the applicant and other accused persons without discussing the probability of the commission of offences and it is only on the basis of the statement of the complainant and her two witnesses without adverting to the probability of the happening of the incident, the summoning order has been passed.
5.

It is further submitted that similarly placed co-accused persons namely Santosh as well as Rustom have been granted bail by the trial Court, vide orders dated 30.11.2021 and 26.09.2022 passed in Bail Application No. 3302 of 2021 and 2473 of 2022.

entities.text: Bail Application No. 3302 of 2021 and 2473 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 6. It is further submitted that police report was submitted by the police stating that earlier court-marriage was solemnized by the instant applicant with victim and it has also come in the rejection order of the Court below of date 21.01.2023 that the applicant and victim were living as husband and wife and due to some strained relations the marriage was desolved by the instrumentality of the Court.
7. It is also submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 16.01.2023 and he is not having any criminal history.
He undertakes that he will cooperate in the early disposal of the complaint case pending before the trial Court.
There is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
8. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

9. Ms. Mansi Gupta, learned counsel appearing for the complainant/informant vehemently opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant is the main accused and he cannot claim parity with the other two accused persons who have been granted bail by the trial Court.

10. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that earlier an F.I.R. was lodged under the orders of the Magistrate passed under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
and was investigated and after thorough investigation a 'closure report/Final Report' was submitted by the investigating officer and on a 'protest petition' filed by the informant/complainant, the same was treated as complaint and the trial Court after recording the statement of the complainant and her witnesses summoned the applicant to face trial under Section 363 and 376 I.P.C. along with co-accused persons namely Santosh Kumar and Rustom, who have already been granted bail by the trial Court.
However, the bail application of the instant applicant has been rejected.

The rejection order passed by the Special Judge, S.C./S.T. Act, Hardoi of date 21.01.2023 would reveal that the 'police report' was submitted with regard to the fact that the applicant had solemnized marriage with the victim and they were living as husband and wife and when they got matrimonial strained relations, their marriage was also resolved through the instrumentality of Court.

2 11.
Let the disputed facts be decided by the trial Court.

However, having regrd to all facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting anything on the merits and demerits of this case, in the considered opinion of this Court, having regard to the period of incarceration already undergone by the instant applicant and also keeping in view that the instant case is a complaint case, in the considered opinion of this Court, the facility of bail may be extended to the applicant, moreover,
when he is not having any criminal history.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

13. Let the accused/applicant- Anil Kumar involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
